title: Cluster 03 DRILL: The Molecular Basis of Cancer, and Stem Cells
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 3 · 10 questions · 104 marks · 35 parts · one mark per minute, so about an hour and three quarters · every question is an actual exam paper question
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE; a right answer said confidently moves on.

Every question below is a real exam paper question. The stem is the paper's own wording. Where a stem has been edited it is only so that it stands without the parts of the original that came before it, and the edit is written out in the Sources block at the foot of that question. If you cannot trace a question to a paper, it is not in here.

Ten questions, 104 marks, 35 parts. The set is sized for coverage, not for the clock. Every learning outcome this cluster owns is tested more than once, from a different angle each time, because this is your first pass over the material. Questions 1 to 5 are cancer, 48 marks; questions 6 to 10 are stem cells and the two places the two halves meet, 56 marks. Two sittings is the intended way to run it.

Question 1 is the whole of 9477 Specimen Paper 2 Question 3, all five parts, at its real 12 marks, with all three of its real figures. Question 5 and Question 8 are Section B essays from real prelim papers at their real 10 marks each; Question 8 is your own school's 2023 Paper 3. Question 6(a) and Question 7(a) are 9477 Specimen Paper 3 Question 3(a), which opens on lymphoid stem cells.

Six real figures. Three are the specimen's own, extracted from the paper. Three are figures from your own Book 3 chapters, used where the paper's figure could not be recovered but the question needs a diagram of that exact thing; each caption says which is which.

Two MCQs, both real, both audited. The paper awards one mark for the letter. The drill then asks you to explain your answer, which is where you have to say whether every option is right and why.

Two errors in your own chapter are built into this drill. Chapter 3.4 page 14 calls embryonic stem cells totipotent, claiming each cell of the early blastocyst could by itself become a healthy individual. It is wrong; pages 8, 13 and 16 of the same chapter are right, and Q6(b) and Q6(c) are built so that believing page 14 costs you marks twice. Chapter 3.4 page 11 says the myeloid progenitor can generate all the different types of blood cell. It cannot; it cannot make lymphocytes, and page 20 gets it right. Q7(e) is built so that believing page 11 costs you marks.

What the marks reward. Every mutation answer starts at the gene and runs base sequence to amino acid sequence to three-dimensional conformation to protein function. Cancer answers run forwards from the mutation; two examiner comments in here penalise arguing back from the wild type. The lexicon is strict: allele not gene, long-term self-renewal not divides indefinitely, lymphoid stem cell not blood stem cell or adult stem cell, and secondary tumours at distant sites or it is invasion and not metastasis.

Out of scope, so nowhere in here. Telomerase, iPSCs, therapeutic cloning, SCNT, and every ethical argument. Apoptosis appears only inside p53's own mechanism.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required answers as well as duplicated labels. Q1 the two routes from a proto-oncogene to an oncogene, read off real sequence and translocation data · Q2 the recessive, two-hit, dosage logic of tumour suppressor genes · Q3 why a mutation usually does not give cancer · Q4 what makes one tumour lethal, angiogenesis and metastasis · Q5 the causative factors, argued from the reverse direction · Q6 potency and the defining features of stem cells · Q7 the blood lineage, lymphoid against myeloid · Q8 the whole mutation-to-cancer pathway produced from memory · Q9 infection and lost immunity as causes · Q10 what distinguishes the stem cell types, and why each is the right clinical tool. Where an outcome is touched twice the two questions need different paragraphs of recall. Q8 is a synthesis essay by design and revisits ground covered earlier, which is why it is placed after the questions it draws on.

Why so much of this drill is figure-led. Data and figure interpretation is 33.5 per cent of the Book 3 corpus and 35.9 per cent of it is figure, table or micrograph led. Any drill for this Book that is mostly text-only is not modelling the exam.
